1	# Protocol B (r2) — minimal, neutral scoping of candidate norm-provenance channels
2	
3	**Goal (from QUESTIONS.md):** decide, for a *bounded* list of locally checkable, read-only
4	channel types, whether any could be an **independent** record of *which norm was in force at
5	time t*. "Independent" = controlled by someone/something other than (a) the norm-maker,
6	(b) the executor of the work, (c) the ruling asserting its own effect. Existence/scoping only —
7	**no archaeology**, no evidence acquisition, **never a forced negative**.
8	
9	The research programme's own artefacts (`docs/knowledgeos/**`) are **never** candidates
10	(self-contamination) and are excluded by the classifier and from E.
11	
12	## 1. Candidate channels (exact patterns)
13	
14	Doc-like ext = `md,markdown,txt,rst,json,ya?ml,toml,csv,tsv`. Every token match below uses a leading
15	`(^|/)` and a trailing token boundary `([._/-]|$)`.
16	
17	| Id | What | Path pattern / source (case-insensitive) |
18	|----|------|-------------------------------------------|
19	| `K-CI` | CI definitions | `.github/workflows/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.circleci/**`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.drone.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.woodpecker*` |
20	| `K-HOOK` | repo-shipped git hooks | `.githooks/**`, `.husky/**`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.lefthook.yml` |
21	| `K-CODEOWNERS` | ownership / branch-protection hints in repo | path basename `CODEOWNERS` |
22	| `K-NORMREG` | norm register / rulings register / in-force record (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`) | doc-like ext and path matching the **register regex** `(^|/)(rulings?|register|registry|decisions?|norm|inforce|authoriz(ation|ations)?)([._/-]|$)` |
23	| `K-STATUS` | the **remaining** status / progress / approval / sign-off records (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`); **disjoint** from `K-NORMREG` | doc-like ext, **not** `K-NORMREG`, path matching a token in {`program_status,status,ruling(s),register,registry,decision(s),adoption(s),approval(s),signoff(s),progress,inforce,norm`}, e.g. `docs/implementation/PROGRAM_STATUS.md` |
24	| `K-DEPLOY` | deployment / config **state** | path token in {`deploy,deployment,release,environment,env,infra,terraform`} or ext `tfstate` |
25	| `K-SIG` | signed commits / tags | **presence** of `gpgsig` header / `-----BEGIN (PGP\|SSH) SIGNATURE-----`; keyring **not** consulted, signatures **not** verified |
26	| `K-LOCALHOOK` | local hooks (`LOCAL_ONLY`) | `.git/hooks/<standard-name>` present, or `core.hooksPath` set |
27	
28	**Host-side channels — `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`** (host not authorized): `K-HOST-AUDIT`
29	(server audit logs), `K-HOST-BRANCHPROT` (branch-protection *enforcement*), `K-HOST-PR-APPROVALS`
30	(PR approvals), `K-CI-RUNS` (CI run history), `K-HOST-MEMBERS` (org/team membership).
31	
32	**The one tip set (B1, N5, N12).** Every history query (paths, W, commit counts, E, N_c, K-SIG)
33	runs over **one** tip file via `git log --stdin` / `git rev-list --stdin`. Tips = refs under
34	`refs/heads/**`, `refs/remotes/**`, `refs/tags/**` only (`refs/stash`, `refs/notes/**` excluded);
35	tags are peeled (`^{commit}`), and **only commit-type tips** are kept. The result does not depend
36	on the checked-out HEAD. Paths are read with `ls-tree -r -z` (N9).
37	
38	## 2. Deterministic answer rules
39	
40	Scope = the **tip set only**; completeness vs the host is never shown. `ND` =
41	`NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK`, `IND` = `INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE`. If a path channel
42	has **0** paths in the tip trees → Q1 = `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` (it may still exist in history
43	behind the tips) and Q2..Q8 = `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`; same label for `K-SIG` when no signature is
44	present in commits reachable from the tips or in tag objects at the tips; `K-LOCALHOOK` uses
45	`NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY`. Host rows are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` for all eight.
46	
47	- **Q1 exists** → `YES_IN_CAPTURE` | `YES_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`) | `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` | `NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY` | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
48	- **Q2 records** → by **type** only: `CONFIG_RULE` (K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-LOCALHOOK), `NORM_REGISTER_RECORD` (K-NORMREG), `STATUS_RECORD` (K-STATUS), `STATE_RECORD_BY_TYPE` (K-DEPLOY), `IDENTITY_ATTESTATION` (K-SIG); content not read.
49	- **Q3 controls** → `CONTROLLED_BY_WRITERS[n=…]` (count only) | for `K-SIG` `ND(keyring not consulted)` | `LOCAL_MACHINE` (`K-LOCALHOOK`).
50	- **Q4 timestamps independent** → `NO_CLIENT_SET` (git recording times are client-generated; a self-attested timestamp is **not** independence). Content timestamps = `ND`.
51	- **Q5 norm-in-force at t** → `ND` for **every** channel: no channel's content is read, and existence never decides this. (`NO_BY_TYPE` removed.)
52	- **Q6 completeness** → `ND[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]`. **Q6 has a single outcome by design**: the check is existence-only over the tip set, so completeness vs the host can never be shown.
53	- **Q7 independence** → see §3. Reachable: `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`, `IND[…]`, `NOT_INDEPENDENT[…]`, `SELF_ATTESTED[…]`, `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`, `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
54	- **Q8 reproducible** → `YES_LOCAL` (content-addressed, rerunnable on the same tip set) | `NO_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`, unversioned) | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
55	
56	## 3. Independence rule (count overlap only)
57	
58	All sets use the **author** e-mail `%ae` only (never `%ce`), lower-cased, over non-merge commits
59	reachable from the one tip set. Every W, E and N_c `git log` call uses `--full-history` (NB-1), so
60	no history simplification prunes commits. Identities never leave a private temp dir; only counts do.
61	
62	- **W_c** = authors of commits touching candidate c's own paths.
63	- **E** (executors) = authors of commits touching the **CODE / TEST roots of Protocol A r1**:
64	  `app/ routes/ database/ resources/ config/ bootstrap/ lang/ public/ tests/`. Root pathspecs are
65	  used, so historic, renamed and deleted paths under those roots count. **Excluded** (as
66	  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob
67	  translation of the classifier, not the tip path names) and `docs/knowledgeos/**`. Doc and
68	  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,
69	  `scripts/`, `storage/`, READMEs) are **not** executor paths.
70	- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).
71	- **N_c** = authors of commits touching the norm-register paths **minus c's own paths**. N is
72	  never derived from the candidate's own paths. For `K-STATUS` (disjoint from `K-NORMREG` by
73	  construction) N_c = all `K-NORMREG` paths; for `K-NORMREG` N_c's path set is empty.
74	- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).
75	
76	Mapping, applied in this order:
77	1. `K-NORMREG` → `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=…]`. This is a **definitional outcome,
78	   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
79	   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
80	   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
81	   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
82	2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
83	3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
84	   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
85	4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
86	5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`
87	   (an **observed** cross-role authorship).
88	6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
89	   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author
90	   identity is observed; it does not show who controls the channel on the host).
91	
92	**Channels that can reach a positive Q7 (NB-10):** only `K-STATUS` and `K-DEPLOY` (the observable
93	channels, rules 4–6), and only when at least one `K-NORMREG` path exists outside their own paths.
94	`K-NORMREG` is always `SELF_ATTESTED`; `K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`, `K-SIG` and `K-LOCALHOOK` are
95	always `IND`. The positive therefore rests on two channel types.
96	
97	**Disclosed limits of §3:** identity aliases (one person, several e-mails) are **not** resolved, so
98	overlaps may be undercounted and the positive is qualified accordingly; a rename commit spanning a
99	code root and a channel path is still counted in E (and in W_c).
100	
101	## 4. Completeness rule
102	
103	**Checkable locally:** existence of the paths/hooks above in the tip set; per-channel commit count,
104	writer **count** and signature **presence**; writer-overlap counts. **Not checkable locally
105	(declared):** branch-protection enforcement, PR approvals, server audit logs, CI run history, org
106	membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
107	are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule
108	or record *says*) is `ND` because content is not read.
109	
110	## 5. Output (written by `scope_b.sh` into an empty `$OUT` outside the repo)
111	
112	- `60_channel_metrics.tsv` — per channel (`K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY`): `channel, paths, commits, writers, overlap_exec, overlap_norm, norm_paths_c, norm_writers_c` (counts only).
113	- `61_path_ids.tsv` — `16-hex-id → channel` (no path strings leave the repo).
114	- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
115	- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
116	- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
117	- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
118	  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
119	  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;
120	  3. `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED` — else ≥1 Q7 = `NOT_INDEPENDENT…` (observed overlap only);
121	  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local
122	     candidates are self-attested records (definitional, §3 rule 1); **no** independence outcome was
123	     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in
124	     `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED`;
125	  5. `LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED` — else (all local rows `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`).
126	
127	  The headline covers local channels only; host channels stay `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`. Also:
128	  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
129	- `00_script.sha256`, `00_env.tsv` (incl. `repo_local_config=READABLE`), `00_errors.tsv`, and `SHA256SUMS` over every emitted file.
130	
131	**Guarantees:** read-only; `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC`; config isolation (N4, NB-2): system/global config off,
132	`GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` unset,
133	`GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (neutralizes `.git/info/grafts`), and every git call gets `-c log.follow=false
134	-c diff.renames=false -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`
135	(plus `core.quotepath=off`, `log.mailmap=false`, `color.ui=never`); **the repo-local config stays
136	readable** (declared). No `set -e` (explicit exits 0/1/2/3); own absolute path resolved+hashed
137	**before** the one `cd`; refuses any `$OUT` inside the work tree or `.git`; emits **counts only** —
138	no names, emails, ref names, URLs, owners or path strings. A final `identity_guard` greps `$OUT` for
139	`@`/signature markers and fails **closed**: a hit → `FAIL`, any grep error (rc ≥ 2) → `FAIL(grep_rc)`,
140	both exit 1. The **only** content read beyond existence/size/counts is commit/tag object headers for
141	**signature presence** (Q1/Q2/Q7 for `K-SIG` strictly require it); no file blob is read.
142	
143	## 6. Disclosed limitations (not fixed)
144	
145	- **N7:** `cat-file` errors in the signature loops are not checked (failures count as unsigned); tags are counted per ref, not per object; x509 `SIGNED MESSAGE` tag signatures are missed.
146	- **N8:** in a linked worktree, OUT is checked against the per-worktree gitdir only, not `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.
147	- **N10:** path IDs are unsalted SHA-256 prefixes, so predictable paths can be reversed by dictionary (no identity leak).
148	- **N11:** `$TMP` holds plaintext e-mails (removed on EXIT, not on SIGKILL); `mkdir -p` may create missing parents of OUT.
149	- **N13:** remaining protocol/script mismatches: Q4 omits the content-timestamp qualifier in the output; K-SIG carries no overlap counts; K-LOCALHOOK Q4 = `NONE`; Q8 shows reproducibility, not independent verification; script length.
150	- **N15:** only top-level `docs/knowledgeos/` is excluded as self-contamination; whether `.claude/` / `claude/` hold programme artefacts is not checked.
151	- **NB-4:** READMEs and other markdown *inside* the code roots (e.g. `tests/README.md`) still count as executor work in E.
152	- **NB-5:** under `pipefail`, a commit object larger than the pipe buffer can make `cat-file | awk` fail on SIGPIPE, so a signed commit counts as unsigned (N7 family).
153	- **NB-6:** on an identity-guard `FAIL` the files stay in OUT; only the exit code and the `FAIL` line signal it, so the consumer must honour the exit code.
154	- **NB-7:** in a linked worktree, K-LOCALHOOK checks the per-worktree `$GD/hooks`, not the common dir's hooks (N8 family).
155	- **NB-8:** no cap on per-path `git log` passes or per-commit `cat-file` spawns; a large K-DEPLOY match multiplies the runtime (performance, not safety).
156	- **NB-9:** one sweeping commit (repo-wide reformat/move) puts its author into W_c, N_c and E at once; that overlap is observed, not forced, but it can dominate the counts.
157

- **Q8 reproducible** → `YES_LOCAL` (content-addressed, rerunnable on the same tip set) | `NO_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`, unversioned) | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.

## 3. Independence rule (count overlap only)

All sets use the **author** e-mail `%ae` only (never `%ce`), lower-cased, over non-merge commits
reachable from the one tip set. Every W, E and N_c `git log` call uses `--full-history` (NB-1), so
no history simplification prunes commits. Identities never leave a private temp dir; only counts do.

- **W_c** = authors of commits touching candidate c's own paths.
- **E** (executors) = authors of commits touching the **CODE / TEST roots of Protocol A r1**:
  `app/ routes/ database/ resources/ config/ bootstrap/ lang/ public/ tests/`. Root pathspecs are
  used, so historic, renamed and deleted paths under those roots count. **Excluded** (as
  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob
  translation of the classifier, not the tip path names) and `docs/knowledgeos/**`. Doc and
  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,
  `scripts/`, `storage/`, READMEs) are **not** executor paths.
- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).
- **N_c** = authors of commits touching the norm-register paths **minus c's own paths**. N is
  never derived from the candidate's own paths. For `K-STATUS` (disjoint from `K-NORMREG` by
  construction) N_c = all `K-NORMREG` paths; for `K-NORMREG` N_c's path set is empty.
- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).

Mapping, applied in this order:
1. `K-NORMREG` → `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=…]`. This is a **definitional outcome,
   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`
   (an **observed** cross-role authorship).
6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author
   identity is observed; it does not show who controls the channel on the host).

**Channels that can reach a positive Q7 (NB-10):** only `K-STATUS` and `K-DEPLOY` (the observable
channels, rules 4–6), and only when at least one `K-NORMREG` path exists outside their own paths.
`K-NORMREG` is always `SELF_ATTESTED`; `K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`, `K-SIG` and `K-LOCALHOOK` are
always `IND`. The positive therefore rests on two channel types.

**Disclosed limits of §3:** identity aliases (one person, several e-mails) are **not** resolved, so
overlaps may be undercounted and the positive is qualified accordingly; a rename commit spanning a
code root and a channel path is still counted in E (and in W_c).

## 4. Completeness rule

**Checkable locally:** existence of the paths/hooks above in the tip set; per-channel commit count,
writer **count** and signature **presence**; writer-overlap counts. **Not checkable locally
(declared):** branch-protection enforcement, PR approvals, server audit logs, CI run history, org
membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule
or record *says*) is `ND` because content is not read.

## 5. Output (written by `scope_b.sh` into an empty `$OUT` outside the repo)

- `60_channel_metrics.tsv` — per channel (`K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY`): `channel, paths, commits, writers, overlap_exec, overlap_norm, norm_paths_c, norm_writers_c` (counts only).
- `61_path_ids.tsv` — `16-hex-id → channel` (no path strings leave the repo).
- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;
  3. `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED` — else ≥1 Q7 = `NOT_INDEPENDENT…` (observed overlap only);
  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local
     candidates are self-attested records (definitional, §3 rule 1); **no** independence outcome was
     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in
     `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED`;
  5. `LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED` — else (all local rows `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`).

  The headline covers local channels only; host channels stay `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`. Also:
  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
- `00_script.sha256`, `00_env.tsv` (incl. `repo_local_config=READABLE`), `00_errors.tsv`, and `SHA256SUMS` over every emitted file.

**Guarantees:** read-only; `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC`; config isolation (N4, NB-2): system/global config off,
`GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` unset,
`GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (neutralizes `.git/info/grafts`), and every git call gets `-c log.follow=false
-c diff.renames=false -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`
(plus `core.quotepath=off`, `log.mailmap=false`, `color.ui=never`); **the repo-local config stays
readable** (declared). No `set -e` (explicit exits 0/1/2/3); own absolute path resolved+hashed
**before** the one `cd`; refuses any `$OUT` inside the work tree or `.git`; emits **counts only** —
no names, emails, ref names, URLs, owners or path strings. A final `identity_guard` greps `$OUT` for
`@`/signature markers and fails **closed**: a hit → `FAIL`, any grep error (rc ≥ 2) → `FAIL(grep_rc)`,
both exit 1. The **only** content read beyond existence/size/counts is commit/tag object headers for
**signature presence** (Q1/Q2/Q7 for `K-SIG` strictly require it); no file blob is read.

## 6. Disclosed limitations (not fixed)

- **N7:** `cat-file` errors in the signature loops are not checked (failures count as unsigned); tags are counted per ref, not per object; x509 `SIGNED MESSAGE` tag signatures are missed.
- **N8:** in a linked worktree, OUT is checked against the per-worktree gitdir only, not `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`.
- **N10:** path IDs are unsalted SHA-256 prefixes, so predictable paths can be reversed by dictionary (no identity leak).
- **N11:** `$TMP` holds plaintext e-mails (removed on EXIT, not on SIGKILL); `mkdir -p` may create missing parents of OUT.
- **N13:** remaining protocol/script mismatches: Q4 omits the content-timestamp qualifier in the output; K-SIG carries no overlap counts; K-LOCALHOOK Q4 = `NONE`; Q8 shows reproducibility, not independent verification; script length.
- **N15:** only top-level `docs/knowledgeos/` is excluded as self-contamination; whether `.claude/` / `claude/` hold programme artefacts is not checked.
- **NB-4:** READMEs and other markdown *inside* the code roots (e.g. `tests/README.md`) still count as executor work in E.
- **NB-5:** under `pipefail`, a commit object larger than the pipe buffer can make `cat-file | awk` fail on SIGPIPE, so a signed commit counts as unsigned (N7 family).
- **NB-6:** on an identity-guard `FAIL` the files stay in OUT; only the exit code and the `FAIL` line signal it, so the consumer must honour the exit code.
- **NB-7:** in a linked worktree, K-LOCALHOOK checks the per-worktree `$GD/hooks`, not the common dir's hooks (N8 family).
- **NB-8:** no cap on per-path `git log` passes or per-commit `cat-file` spawns; a large K-DEPLOY match multiplies the runtime (performance, not safety).
- **NB-9:** one sweeping commit (repo-wide reformat/move) puts its author into W_c, N_c and E at once; that overlap is observed, not forced, but it can dominate the counts.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scope_b.sh (r2) -- Protocol B scoping. Read-only; existence/metadata only. No network, no host access.
# Emits COUNTS ONLY: no names, emails, ref names, URLs or path strings leave TMP; paths -> 16-hex ids.
# The ONLY content read beyond existence/counts is commit/tag object headers for signature PRESENCE
# (Q1/Q2/Q7 for K-SIG strictly require it); no file blob is ever read.
# Usage (from anywhere inside the working clone):  OUT=/abs/empty/dir bash scope_b.sh
# Exit: 0 ok | 1 ok-with-unexpected-codes or identity-guard fail | 2 refused | 3 capture invalid
set -u -o pipefail
export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC GIT_PAGER=cat PAGER=cat GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
  GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null  # NB-2: neutralizes .git/info/grafts
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_NAMESPACE GIT_COMMON_DIR \
  GIT_CONFIG GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS GIT_CONFIG_COUNT   # N4/NB-2: no injected config; repo-local config stays readable (declared)
die() { printf 'scope_b: %s\n' "$2" >&2; exit "$1"; }

# ---- resolve OWN absolute path and hash it BEFORE any cd (corrects earlier relative-BASH_SOURCE defect) ----
SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; case "$SELF" in /*) ;; *) SELF="$PWD/$SELF" ;; esac
SELF="$(realpath -- "$SELF")" || die 2 "cannot resolve own path"
SELFSHA="$(sha256sum < "$SELF" | cut -d' ' -f1)" || die 2 "cannot hash self"
# N4: these overrides are passed to EVERY git call
git() { command git -c core.quotepath=off -c log.mailmap=false -c color.ui=never -c log.follow=false -c diff.renames=false \
  -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false "$@"; }

# ---- preconditions (exit 2) ----
OUT="${OUT:-}"; [ -n "$OUT" ] || die 2 "OUT not set"
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) die 2 "OUT must be an absolute path" ;; esac
[ "$(git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null)" = true ] || die 2 "not inside a work tree"
[ "$(git rev-parse --is-bare-repository 2>/dev/null)" = false ] || die 2 "bare repository"
TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || die 2 "no toplevel"
GD="$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)" || die 2 "no git dir"
OUT="$(realpath -m -- "$OUT")" || die 2 "realpath OUT failed"
TOPR="$(realpath -- "$TOP")"; GDR="$(realpath -- "$GD")"
for d in "$TOPR" "$GDR"; do case "$OUT/" in "$d"/*) die 2 "OUT must be outside the work tree and .git" ;; esac; done
if [ -e "$OUT" ]; then { [ -d "$OUT" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A -- "$OUT")" ]; } || die 2 "OUT must be an empty directory"; fi
TMP="$(mktemp -d)" || die 2 "mktemp failed"; TMP="$(realpath -- "$TMP")"
case "$TMP/" in "$TOPR"/*|"$GDR"/*|"$OUT"/*) rm -rf -- "$TMP"; die 2 "TMPDIR must be outside the repo and OUT" ;; esac
trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMP"' EXIT
mkdir -p -- "$OUT" || die 2 "cannot create OUT"
cd -- "$TOP" || die 2 "cannot cd to the toplevel"   # the one and only cd; self already resolved+hashed above

ERR="$OUT/00_errors.tsv"; : > "$ERR"; : > "$TMP/e"
ok() { local l="$1" rc="$2" a; shift 2; for a in "$@"; do [ "$rc" = "$a" ] && return 0; done; printf '%s\t%s\n' "$l" "$rc" >> "$ERR"; return 1; }

ND=NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK; IND=INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE
finish() { ( cd -- "$OUT" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS -print | sort | xargs -r -d '\n' sha256sum ) > "$OUT/SHA256SUMS"; exit "$1"; }

  tag) git rev-parse --verify -q "$o^{commit}" < /dev/null >> "$TMP/t0" 2>>"$TMP/e"; ok peel $? 0 1 ;; esac; done < "$TMP/refs"

  ok lstree "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" 0; done < "$TMP/tips"
sort -u "$TMP/paths" > "$TMP/pu"; mv "$TMP/pu" "$TMP/paths"

# ---- classify candidate channels (bounded vocabulary; docs/knowledgeos excluded) ----
# BLK-1/NB-3: K-NORMREG (register regex, trailing token boundary) and K-STATUS (the remaining status records) are disjoint
awk -F'\t' '
{ p=$0; q=tolower(p); b=q; sub(/.*\//,"",b)
  if (q ~ /^docs\/knowledgeos\//) next

    nc=$((nc + $(awk 'END{print NR}' "$TMP/w1"))); cat "$TMP/w1" >> "$TMP/W"

# Protocol B (r3) — minimal, neutral scoping of candidate norm-provenance channels

**Goal (from QUESTIONS.md):** decide, for a *bounded* list of locally checkable, read-only
channel types, whether any could be an **independent** record of *which norm was in force at
time t*. "Independent" = controlled by someone/something other than (a) the norm-maker,
(b) the executor of the work, (c) the ruling asserting its own effect. Existence/scoping only —
**no archaeology**, no evidence acquisition, **never a forced negative**.

The research programme's own artefacts (`docs/knowledgeos/**`) are **never** candidates
(self-contamination) and are excluded by the classifier and from E.

## 1. Candidate channels (exact patterns)

Doc-like ext = `md,markdown,txt,rst,json,ya?ml,toml,csv,tsv`. Every token match below (K-NORMREG,
K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY) uses the leading boundary `(^|[/._-])` and the trailing token boundary `([._/-]|$)`
(BLK-2). A token can therefore start a path segment, or it can follow `.`, `_` or `-` inside a name
(e.g. `ADR-0007-Rulings.md`, `PROGRAM_STATUS.md`). It must end at `.`, `_`, `/`, `-` or the end of the path.

| Id | What | Path pattern / source (case-insensitive) |
|----|------|-------------------------------------------|
| `K-CI` | CI definitions | `.github/workflows/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.circleci/**`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.drone.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.woodpecker*` |
| `K-HOOK` | repo-shipped git hooks | `.githooks/**`, `.husky/**`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.lefthook.yml` |
| `K-CODEOWNERS` | ownership / branch-protection hints in repo | path basename `CODEOWNERS` |
| `K-NORMREG` | norm register / rulings register / in-force record (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`) | doc-like ext and path matching the **register regex** `(^|[/._-])(rulings?|register|registry|decisions?|norm|inforce|authoriz(ation|ations)?)([._/-]|$)` |
| `K-STATUS` | the **remaining** status / progress / approval / sign-off records (**outside** `docs/knowledgeos/`); **disjoint** from `K-NORMREG` | doc-like ext, **not** `K-NORMREG`, path matching `(^|[/._-])`+token+`([._/-]|$)` for a token in {`program_status,status,ruling(s),register,registry,decision(s),adoption(s),approval(s),signoff(s),progress,inforce,norm`}, e.g. `docs/implementation/PROGRAM_STATUS.md` |
| `K-DEPLOY` | deployment / config **state** | path token (`(^|[/._-])`+token+`([._/-]|$)`) in {`deploy,deployment,release,environment,env,infra,terraform`} or ext `tfstate` |
| `K-SIG` | signed commits / tags | **presence** of `gpgsig` header / `-----BEGIN (PGP\|SSH) SIGNATURE-----`; keyring **not** consulted, signatures **not** verified |
| `K-LOCALHOOK` | local hooks (`LOCAL_ONLY`) | `.git/hooks/<standard-name>` present, or `core.hooksPath` set |

**E-exclusion globs = classifier regex, by construction (BLK-2).** For each doc token t (the union
of the K-NORMREG and K-STATUS tokens, with `authoriz`, `authorization`, `authorizations` written out) and
each doc ext x, E excludes (`:(exclude,glob,icase)`):
- token at segment start: `**/$t.$x`, `**/$t[._-]*.$x`, `**/$t/**/*.$x`, `**/$t[._-]*/**/*.$x`;
- token after `.`/`_`/`-`: `**/*[._-]$t.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t[._-]*.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t/**/*.$x`, `**/*[._-]$t[._-]*/**/*.$x`.

For each K-DEPLOY token t it excludes `**/$t`, `**/$t/**`, `**/$t[._-]*`, `**/$t[._-]*/**`, the same four
forms with `*[._-]` in front of t, and also `**/*.tfstate`.

The glob set and the regex are **equivalent by construction**. Each glob form is exactly one case of
the regex:
- the leading boundary is either `^`/`/` (→ `**/`) or `.`/`_`/`-` (→ `**/*[._-]`);
- the trailing boundary is one of: the extension dot of the basename (→ `.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside the
  basename (→ `[._-]*.$x`); `/` (→ `/**/*.$x`); `.`/`_`/`-` inside a directory segment (→ `[._-]*/**/*.$x`).

For doc tokens, the path-end case `$` cannot occur: the path must end in `.$x`, and no token is a doc
extension. For K-DEPLOY, the path-end case is the bare `$t` form. The construction relies on these git
wildmatch semantics: `*` does not cross `/`; `**/` and `/**/` match zero or more directories; `icase`
is ASCII case folding, like awk `tolower` under `LC_ALL=C`. **No residual mismatch is known at the
pattern level.** The equivalence is argued, not executed. By design (§3), the globs are applied to
historic paths and the regex to tip paths.

**Host-side channels — `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`** (host not authorized): `K-HOST-AUDIT`
(server audit logs), `K-HOST-BRANCHPROT` (branch-protection *enforcement*), `K-HOST-PR-APPROVALS`
(PR approvals), `K-CI-RUNS` (CI run history), `K-HOST-MEMBERS` (org/team membership).

**The one tip set (B1, N5, N12).** Every history query (paths, W, commit counts, E, N_c, K-SIG)
runs over **one** tip file via `git log --stdin` / `git rev-list --stdin`. Tips = refs under
`refs/heads/**`, `refs/remotes/**`, `refs/tags/**` only (`refs/stash`, `refs/notes/**` excluded);
tags are peeled (`^{commit}`), and **only commit-type tips** are kept. The result does not depend
on the checked-out HEAD. Paths are read with `ls-tree -r -z` (N9).

## 2. Deterministic answer rules

Scope = the **tip set only**; completeness vs the host is never shown. `ND` =
`NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK`, `IND` = `INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE`. If a path channel
has **0** paths in the tip trees → Q1 = `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` (it may still exist in history
behind the tips) and Q2..Q8 = `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`; same label for `K-SIG` when no signature is
present in commits reachable from the tips or in tag objects at the tips; `K-LOCALHOOK` uses
`NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY`. Host rows are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` for all eight.

- **Q1 exists** → `YES_IN_CAPTURE` | `YES_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`) | `NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS` | `NOT_EVIDENCED_LOCALLY` | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
- **Q2 records** → by **type** only: `CONFIG_RULE` (K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-LOCALHOOK), `NORM_REGISTER_RECORD` (K-NORMREG), `STATUS_RECORD` (K-STATUS), `STATE_RECORD_BY_TYPE` (K-DEPLOY), `IDENTITY_ATTESTATION` (K-SIG); content not read.
- **Q3 controls** → `CONTROLLED_BY_WRITERS[n=…]` (count only) | for `K-SIG` `ND(keyring not consulted)` | `LOCAL_MACHINE` (`K-LOCALHOOK`).
- **Q4 timestamps independent** → `NO_CLIENT_SET` (git recording times are client-generated; a self-attested timestamp is **not** independence). Content timestamps = `ND`.
- **Q5 norm-in-force at t** → `ND` for **every** channel: no channel's content is read, and existence never decides this. (`NO_BY_TYPE` removed.)
- **Q6 completeness** → `ND[COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN]`. **Q6 has a single outcome by design**: the check is existence-only over the tip set, so completeness vs the host can never be shown.
- **Q7 independence** → see §3. Reachable: `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`, `IND[…]`, `NOT_INDEPENDENT[…]`, `SELF_ATTESTED[…]`, `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`, `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.
- **Q8 reproducible** → `YES_LOCAL` (content-addressed, rerunnable on the same tip set) | `NO_LOCAL_ONLY` (`K-LOCALHOOK`, unversioned) | `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`.

## 3. Independence rule (count overlap only)

All sets use the **author** e-mail `%ae` only (never `%ce`), lower-cased, over non-merge commits
reachable from the one tip set. Every W, E and N_c `git log` call uses `--full-history` (NB-1), so
no history simplification prunes commits. Identities never leave a private temp dir; only counts do.

- **W_c** = authors of commits touching candidate c's own paths.
- **E** (executors) = authors of commits touching the **CODE / TEST roots of Protocol A r1**:
  `app/ routes/ database/ resources/ config/ bootstrap/ lang/ public/ tests/`. Root pathspecs are
  used, so historic, renamed and deleted paths under those roots count. **Excluded** (as
  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob
  translation of the classifier, not the tip path names) and `docs/knowledgeos/**`. Doc and
  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,
  `scripts/`, `storage/`, READMEs) are **not** executor paths.
- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).
- **N_c** = authors of commits touching the norm-register paths **minus c's own paths**. N is
  never derived from the candidate's own paths. For `K-STATUS` (disjoint from `K-NORMREG` by
  construction) N_c = all `K-NORMREG` paths; for `K-NORMREG` N_c's path set is empty.
- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).

Mapping, applied in this order:
1. `K-NORMREG` → `SELF_ATTESTED[norm_register;overlap_exec=…]`. This is a **definitional outcome,
   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`
   (an **observed** cross-role authorship).
6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author
   identity is observed; it does not show who controls the channel on the host).

**Channels that can reach a positive Q7 (NB-10):** only `K-STATUS` and `K-DEPLOY` (the observable
channels, rules 4–6), and only when at least one `K-NORMREG` path exists outside their own paths.
`K-NORMREG` is always `SELF_ATTESTED`; `K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`, `K-SIG` and `K-LOCALHOOK` are
always `IND`. The positive therefore rests on two channel types.

**Disclosed limits of §3:** identity aliases (one person, several e-mails) are **not** resolved, so
overlaps may be undercounted and the positive is qualified accordingly; a rename commit spanning a
code root and a channel path is still counted in E (and in W_c).

## 4. Completeness rule

**Checkable locally:** existence of the paths/hooks above in the tip set; per-channel commit count,
writer **count** and signature **presence**; writer-overlap counts. **Not checkable locally
(declared):** branch-protection enforcement, PR approvals, server audit logs, CI run history, org
membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule
or record *says*) is `ND` because content is not read.

## 5. Output (written by `scope_b.sh` into an empty `$OUT` outside the repo)

- `60_channel_metrics.tsv` — per channel (`K-CI, K-HOOK, K-CODEOWNERS, K-NORMREG, K-STATUS, K-DEPLOY`): `channel, paths, commits, writers, overlap_exec, overlap_norm, norm_paths_c, norm_writers_c` (counts only).
- `61_path_ids.tsv` — `16-hex-id → channel` (no path strings leave the repo).
- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;
  3. `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED` — else ≥1 Q7 = `NOT_INDEPENDENT…` (observed overlap only);
  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local
     candidates are self-attested records (definitional, §3 rule 1); **no** independence outcome was
     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in
     `LOCAL_NO_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_OBSERVED`;
  5. `LOCAL_NO_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCED` — else (all local rows `NOT_APPLICABLE(Q1)`).

  The headline covers local channels only; host channels stay `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY`. Also:
  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
- `00_script.sha256`, `00_env.tsv` (incl. `repo_local_config=READABLE`), `00_errors.tsv`, and `SHA256SUMS` over every emitted file.

**Guarantees:** read-only; `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC`; config isolation (N4, NB-2): system/global config off,
`GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` unset,
`GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (neutralizes `.git/info/grafts`), and every git call gets `-c log.follow=false
-c diff.renames=false -c log.decorate=false -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`
(plus `core.quotepath=off`, `log.mailmap=false`, `color.ui=never`); **the repo-local config stays
readable** (declared). Pathspec and trace isolation (NB-11): `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS`,
`GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS` and every `GIT_TRACE*` /
`GIT_TRACE2*` variable are unset. The trace variables are unset by name (`GIT_TRACE`, `GIT_TRACE2`,
`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, `GIT_TRACE2_PERF`, `GIT_TRACE_PACKET`, `GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE`, `GIT_TRACE_SETUP`,
`GIT_TRACE_CURL`, `GIT_TRACE_PACK_ACCESS`) and also by prefix, so any other `GIT_TRACE…` variable is
removed too. No `set -e` (explicit exits 0/1/2/3); own absolute path resolved+hashed
**before** the one `cd`; refuses any `$OUT` inside the work tree or `.git`; emits **counts only** —
no names, emails, ref names, URLs, owners or path strings. A final `identity_guard` greps `$OUT` for
`@`/signature markers and fails **closed**: a hit → `FAIL`, any grep error (rc ≥ 2) → `FAIL(grep_rc)`,
both exit 1. The **only** content read beyond existence/size/counts is commit/tag object headers for
**signature presence** (Q1/Q2/Q7 for `K-SIG` strictly require it); no file blob is read.

  `:(exclude,glob,icase)` pathspecs): every candidate-channel **glob pattern** of §1 (a glob

  governance roots (`docs/`, `developer_guide/`, `engineering/`, `.claude/`, `claude/`,

- **Norm-register paths** = the `K-NORMREG` paths (register regex, §1).

- `overlap_exec = |W_c ∩ E|`, `overlap_norm = |W_c ∩ N_c|` (`NA` when N_c's path set is empty).

   not an observed negative**: by declared definition a register records its own rulings, so it is
   criterion (c), "the ruling asserting its own effect" (QUESTIONS.md: a self-attested record is not
   independent merely for having a timestamp). No data is consulted for this outcome; it is not a
   `NOT_INDEPENDENT` and is never counted as one (§5).
2. N_c's path set is empty → `IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate;…]`.
3. Mechanism **unobservable locally** (`K-CI`, `K-HOOK`, `K-CODEOWNERS`: enforcement is host/client-side;
   `K-SIG`: signatures unverified; `K-LOCALHOOK`: local, unversioned) → `IND` with the overlap counts where computed.
4. Mechanism observable (`K-STATUS`, `K-DEPLOY`: writer set in repo) and any of W_c, N_c, E empty → `IND[empty_set;W=…;N_c=…;E=…]`.
5. Observable, `overlap_norm>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_norm]`; else `overlap_exec>0` → `NOT_INDEPENDENT[overlap_exec]`

6. Observable, W_c ≠ ∅, N_c ≠ ∅, E ≠ ∅ and both overlaps `0` →
   **`INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL[aliases_unresolved]`** (qualified positive: no shared author

membership, host push times, and whether the local ref set is complete vs the host. All of these
are `NOT_CHECKABLE_LOCALLY` / `COMPLETE_VS_HOST=NOT_SHOWN`; the content of any file (what a rule

- `58_signatures.tsv` — `commits_total, commits_signed, tags_signed`.
- `56_local_hooks.tsv` — `standard_hooks_present, core_hooksPath`.
- `70_answers.tsv` — candidate × Q1..Q8 (the §2/§3 mapping), incl. `K-SIG`, `K-LOCALHOOK`, host rows.
- `71_overall.tsv` — `headline` **computed from the per-channel Q7 values** (local rows), first match wins:
  1. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL` — ≥1 Q7 = `INDEPENDENT_AT_IDENTITY_COUNT_LEVEL…`;
  2. `LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_NOT_DETERMINABLE` — else ≥1 Q7 = `IND…`;

  4. `LOCAL_ONLY_SELF_ATTESTED_RECORDS` — else ≥1 Q7 = `SELF_ATTESTED…`: the only evidenced local

     observed, neither positive nor negative. `SELF_ATTESTED` is counted in this bucket only, never in

  `complete_vs_host=NOT_SHOWN`, per-outcome Q7 counts (incl. `self_attested`), `not_evidenced`, `host_channels`, `identity_guard`.
